headline: A 2016 law asks the President each year to call on Americans to observe two minutes of silence on Veterans Day to honor veterans.
what_it_does: The law directs the President to issue a yearly proclamation calling on people in the United States to observe two minutes of silence on Veterans Day. The silence begins at 3:11 p.m. Atlantic standard time. The purpose is to honor the service and sacrifice of veterans throughout the nation's history.
when_it_takes_effect: The law was enacted on October 7, 2016, and the yearly proclamation applies on each Veterans Day after that.
